newsitem.title: UK: East Midlands soars on bid talk.
newsitem.headline: East Midlands soars on bid talk.

text.p: Shares in East Midlands Electricity soared over 11 percent on Wednesday in an otherwise steady market as bid speculation attracted investors, traders said.
East Midlands Electricity shares touched 597p before settling back to 590, up 55p on the day at 1251 GMT. The stock headed the percentage gainers list and almost two million shares had changed hands.
"There's a lot of bid speculation around the stock although no names have been mentioned," one dealer said, echoing others.
Other stocks in the sector were firm, notably PowerGen which gained five pence to 539p.
PowerGen chairman Ed Wallis said on Wednesday he does not expect PowerGen will have to pay any windfall tax levied by a future Labour government on privatised utilities.

"Blair seems to be putting forward a view which says if such a tax is to be applied, it will be applied to those who are in a monopoly business, those who are price regulated and those who have enjoyed the benefits of slack regulation."
"On all three counts, it does not apply to us," he said.
Dealers thought Wallis' comments that the electricity industry was too crowded had fuelled takeover speculation.
